title: Claw — SSH MCP Server: Extend Claude Code Tools to Remote Machines
description: Claw (opsyhq/claw, v0.1.7, npm @opsyhq/claw) is an MCP server that extends Claude Code's native tools (bash, read, write, edit, grep, glob) to any machine accessible via SSH. Ships a small Go binary to the remote machine over SSH; the binary serves as a tool execution proxy. No ports to open, no daemons, no root required — connection is pure SSH. Install: 'claw init --from-ssh' imports machines from ~/.ssh/config. 'claw install claude-code' writes MCP config. Use cases: (1) Check logs on prod without copy-paste. (2) Grep for errors across services. (3) Edit configs on staging. (4) Run scripts on GPU servers. Highly relevant for Tailscale topology: requiem (desktop, primary), orbis-1 (laptop WSL), dashi (phone Termux) — Claw would let Claude Code running on requiem directly operate on orbis-1 or remote servers. Published ~7 days ago. HN Show HN with active discussion. Stars not confirmed but recently launched.
notes: Published ~7 days ago. Highly relevant for the Tailscale device mesh (requiem/orbis-1/dashi). Potential overlap: the existing Tailscale/SSH setup already lets Claude Code SSH into other machines via Bash tool. Claw's value-add is a structured MCP interface vs raw SSH commands — evaluate whether structured tool calls vs 'ssh user@host cmd' is worth the MCP overhead. Check stars after 2 weeks to see traction.
